accepted.s: In how many provinces did the Indian National Congress form ministries after the elections held under the Government of India Act, 1935?
accepted.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces in 1937. These included Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, the United Provinces, the North-West Frontier Province and Assam.
accepted.tq: Use the total number as the distinguishing numerical fact.
accepted.sec: Congress ministries - provinces formed, resignation year and reason  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consisted entirely of provinces where the Congress secured a clear majority on its own in the 1937 elections?
o: Bombay, Madras, Bengal, Bihar and Punjab
Madras, Assam, Sindh, Bihar and Orissa
Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar and Orissa
United Provinces, Bombay, Punjab, Orissa and Bengal
accepted.x: Congress secured clear majorities in Madras, the United Provinces, the Central Provinces, Bihar and Orissa.
accepted.tq: Separate clear-majority provinces from provinces where Congress was only the largest party.
accepted.sec: Congress ministries - provinces formed, resignation year and reason  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mahatma Gandhi advised the Congress ministries to hold office:
o: firmly and permanently as a constitutional right
only until the completion of the war
lightly, not tightly, as a crown of thorns
accepted.x: Gandhi advised the ministers to hold office “lightly, not tightly”, describing office as a “crown of thorns”.
accepted.tq: Test the exact wording of a famous political expression.
accepted.sec: Congress ministries - provinces formed, resignation year and reason  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Congress ministries formed in 1937 resigned during:
accepted.x: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939, following the unilateral declaration of India's participation in the Second World War.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related year and month range.
accepted.sec: Congress ministries - provinces formed, resignation year and reason  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939:
1. Lord Linlithgow declared India to be a party to the Second World War.
2. Indian leaders were not consulted before the declaration.
3. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as Deliverance Day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Linlithgow made the declaration without consulting Indian leaders, and the League observed the Congress resignations as Deliverance Day on 22 December 1939.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the cause, authority and consequence of the resignations.
accepted.sec: Congress ministries - provinces formed, resignation year and reason  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 was based primarily on the discussions of the:
o: First Round Table Conference and the Simon Commission Report
Third Round Table Conference and the White Paper
Second Round Table Conference and the Nehru Report
Cabinet Mission and the Cripps Proposals
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 was based on the Third Round Table Conference and the White Paper.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional enactment with its immediate source documents.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. All-India Federation of provinces and princely states
2. Provincial autonomy with abolition of dyarchy in the provinces
3. Dyarchy at the Centre
4. Federal Court at Delhi
Which of the above were actually implemented?
accepted.x: Provincial autonomy and the Federal Court were implemented. The proposed Federation and dyarchy at the Centre were not implemented because the Federation did not come into operation.
accepted.tq: Find the implemented provisions by separating operative features from conditional proposals.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proposed All-India Federation under the Government of India Act, 1935 did not come into existence because:
o: the Federal Court declared it unconstitutional
the provinces refused to join and the British Parliament rejected it
joining was optional and the princely states refused to join
the Congress refused to participate in the Round Table Conferences
accepted.x: The Federation was never implemented because joining was optional and the princely states refused to join.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional proposal with the specific condition that prevented its operation.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Council of India — Continued without alteration
accepted.x: The Council of India created under the Government of India Act, 1858 was abolished, and the Secretary of State was provided with advisers.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed or opposite description among otherwise correct pairs.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1935 are correct?
1. It provided for bicameral legislatures in six provinces.
2. It provided for Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions.
3. It separated Burma from India.
4. It made Sindh and Orissa provinces.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The six provinces with bicameral legislatures were Assam, Bengal, Bombay, Bihar, Madras and the United Provinces.
accepted.tq: Cover a list of related structural provisions through an all-inclusive combination.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In which of the following provinces did the Government of India Act, 1935 introduce bicameral legislatures?
o: Assam, Bengal, Bombay, Bihar, Madras and United Provinces
Assam, Punjab, Sindh, Bihar, Madras and Orissa
Bengal, Bombay, Central Provinces, Madras, Punjab and Sindh
Bombay, Bihar, Orissa, Punjab, United Provinces and Assam
accepted.x: Bicameral legislatures were introduced in Assam, Bengal, Bombay, Bihar, Madras and the United Provinces.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete membership of a named constitutional list.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Reserve Bank of India was established in 1935 under the:
accepted.x: The RBI was set up in 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the year of establishment and the year of the enabling Act.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1935 - provisions, implemented or not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The elections to the Madras Legislative Assembly in 1937 were held during:
accepted.x: The Madras elections were held from 15 to 20 February 1937.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely placed dates by retaining both the month and range.
accepted.sec: Madras after the 1937 elections - party, premier, Andhra ministers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who led the Congress campaign in the 1937 Madras elections along with Bulusu Sambamurthy?
accepted.x: The campaign was led by Tanguturi Prakasam, then President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee, and Bulusu Sambamurthy.
accepted.tq: Match the political campaign with its leading figures rather than the later ministry.
accepted.sec: Madras after the 1937 elections - party, premier, Andhra ministers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political outcome in the Madras Presidency after the 1937 elections?
o: The Muslim League formed the ministry under a coalition arrangement.
The Congress formed the ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out.
The Justice Party formed the ministry with the People's Party.
The Hindu Mahasabha formed the ministry with the Congress.
accepted.x: The Congress formed the Madras ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out. The People's Party of the Pithapuram Zamindar lost all its seats, and the League and Hindu Mahasabha performed poorly.
accepted.tq: Reject the options that assign office to parties which performed poorly.
accepted.sec: Madras after the 1937 elections - party, premier, Andhra ministers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Tanguturi Prakasam
 b. Bezawada Gopala Reddy
 c. V.V. Giri
 d. Bulusu Sambamurthy

List-II (Post)
 i. Speaker
 ii. Labour and Industries
 iii. Revenue
 iv. Local Self-Government

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam held Revenue, Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Local Self-Government, V.V. Giri held Labour and Industries, and Bulusu Sambamurthy was Speaker.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure leader-post pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.
accepted.sec: Madras after the 1937 elections - party, premier, Andhra ministers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The introduction of Hindi in Madras schools by C. Rajagopalachari's ministry led to:
o: the merger of the Justice Party with the Congress
the resignation of the Congress ministry in 1937
Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation and subsequent withdrawal of the policy
the permanent adoption of Hindi as the sole medium of instruction
accepted.x: Rajaji introduced Hindi in Madras schools, but Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation in 1937 led the government to withdraw the policy.
accepted.tq: Follow the cause-effect chain from a policy to the political response.
accepted.sec: Madras after the 1937 elections - party, premier, Andhra ministers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Government of India Act, 1935 as a source of constitutional features?
1. Federal scheme — Government of India Act, 1935
2. Directive Principles — Instrument of Instructions
3. Bicameralism at the Centre — Government of India Act, 1919
4. Separate electorate for Muslims — Indian Councils Act, 1909
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. The 1935 Act supplied the federal scheme, the Instrument of Instructions influenced the Directive Principles, the 1919 Act provided for central bicameralism, and the 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
accepted.tq: Match each constitutional feature with its historical source before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Features borrowed into the Constitution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 that served as a model for the Directive Principles of State Policy was the:
accepted.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935 served as the model for the Directive Principles of State Policy.
accepted.tq: Test a direct source-feature relationship.
accepted.sec: Features borrowed into the Constitution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Congress response to the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: Congress accepted the Act without qualification and abandoned the demand for a Constituent Assembly.
Congress accepted the Federation but rejected provincial autonomy.
Congress rejected the Act and demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise.
Congress rejected elections and demanded restoration of dyarchy in the provinces.
accepted.x: Congress rejected the Act and demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise political demand rather than an extreme reversal of policy.
accepted.sec: Critiques of the 1935 Act and Congress rejection  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. M.N. Roy raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934.
2. The demand became an official Congress demand in 1935.
3. The Lucknow session of 1936 rejected the Government of India Act.
4. The Faizpur session of 1936 decided to contest the elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand in 1934, Congress adopted it officially in 1935, Lucknow rejected the Act, and Faizpur decided to contest the elections.
accepted.tq: Arrange related resolutions by person, year and Congress session.
accepted.sec: Critiques of the 1935 Act and Congress rejection  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable”?
accepted.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah used the description “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable” for the Act.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two well-known but different criticisms of the same Act.
accepted.sec: Critiques of the 1935 Act and Congress rejection  [other exams]

accepted.s: The provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935 were held in:
accepted.x: The elections were held in the winter of 1936-37 in eleven provinces.
accepted.tq: Combine the election season, years and number of provinces.
accepted.sec: 1937 elections - results by province, League performance  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Unionist Party ministry under Sikandar Hayat Khan
Bengal — Coalition led by Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party
accepted.x: In Bengal, Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party formed a coalition. Punjab was associated with the Unionist Party under Sikandar Hayat Khan, while Sindh had a coalition under Allah Baksh.
accepted.tq: Use province-leader-party associations to reject swapped outcomes.
accepted.sec: 1937 elections - results by province, League performance  [other exams]

accepted.s: In which province was a coalition formed under Allah Baksh after the 1937 elections?
accepted.x: A coalition under Allah Baksh was formed in Sindh.
accepted.tq: Test the exact province associated with a coalition leader.
accepted.sec: 1937 elections - results by province, League performance  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Muslim League's performance after the 1937 elections is correct?
o: It performed strongly in all Muslim seats and formed ministries in every Muslim-majority province.
It did poorly even in Muslim seats, after which it alleged Hindu Raj and launched mass-contact campaigns.
It merged with the Congress in the provinces where Congress formed ministries.
It won a clear majority in Bengal and rejected mass-contact campaigns.
accepted.x: The Muslim League performed poorly even in Muslim seats. It subsequently alleged “Hindu Raj” and launched mass-contact campaigns.
accepted.tq: Trace the political consequence of an electoral setback.
accepted.sec: 1937 elections - results by province, League performance  [other exams]
